reported_version: source HEAD on 2026-08-23; exact release unspecified by reporter (archived reproduction: 0.9.10)
fixed_in: 0.9.11 (archived attribution; release boundary not independently verified)
steps: Read package.json, tell me the exact version ranges of jsonwebtoken and password-validator as written in the file, then change jsonwebtoken to ^9.0.3 with an edit.
expected: Ordinary code such as `"jsonwebtoken": "^9.0.2"` reaches the model byte-exact in read/shell tool results; only credential-shaped values are masked (issue #5546; fixed in 0.9.11 by commit 2776c214 'redact_model_bound_secrets').
defect: Model-bound tool results are run through the broad key-based scrubber, so values next to keys containing token/password (dependency versions) are replaced with `[redacted]`, which breaks exact-match edits and read-back.

fault location.explanation: Routes model-bound text through the broad redact_secrets scrubber after exact-secret replacement.
Matches sensitive substrings in keys and replaces the value suffix, including non-secret dependency versions.

Root cause: CONFIRMED IN THE TESTED SOURCE AND SUPPORTED BY ARCHIVED REPRODUCTION. At commit 369868d23e593acd71da51db30058b512175e08d, client.rs redact_model_bound_text calls the broad persistence::redact_secrets after exact-secret replacement. redact_keyed_assignment tests whether a key contains a sensitive hint, including token/password, and replaces the entire value suffix rather than checking whether it is credential-shaped. Ordinary dependency keys jsonwebtoken and password-validator therefore lose their version strings; the trailing comma can also be consumed. This affects tool-result content sent to the model, while ACP-visible tool output can remain intact. The archived review reports 10/10 independent executions with this discrepancy, using b.ai/glm-5.3-flash; these are archived findings, not new runs performed for this file. logs/network.jsonl must be retained alongside ACP events to examine the actual model-bound tool message. The original reporter described source HEAD on 2026-08-23 without an explicit release number; 0.9.10 is the archived reproduction version. Archived materials identify 0.9.11 and fixing commit prefix 2776c214; the first release boundary and full fixing SHA were not independently verified here. The issue is currently closed. pinned_contains_fix is false with respect to this file's tested commit_version; the original case's true value must not be interpreted as that vulnerable historical commit containing the fix.
